mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2% in a month indicates a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods where RSAFS increased by more than 1% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a strong demand in the housing market, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over a quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% over a quarter.
